_comment: Tier-2 for skfem convection_diffusion#0, a catalog-drift correction. Measured on skfem 12.0.1, MeshTri().refined(2) / ElementTriP1: skfem.helpers.grad(u) and u.grad[i] both assemble to a matrix bit-identical to skfem.models.poisson.laplace (nnz 105, max abs difference exactly 0.0), so the prior 'grad(u) raises NameError' claim is false. What DOES bite is the numpy @ operator on the (dim, n_elem, n_qp) DiscreteField arrays, which raises the gufunc core-dimension ValueError; and a genuinely undefined free function raises the ordinary Python NameError at call time, which is how the two are told apart. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 rewrites the via_matmul form body from grad(u) @ grad(v) to dot(grad(u), grad(v)), the documented fix for the @ pitfall. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 6 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'matmul: Input operand 1 has a mismatch in its core dimension' (and emits the forbidden 'FAIL:'), so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
expect_in_output: matmul: Input operand 1 has a mismatch in its core dimension
